summary: The codes capture local meaning contrasts visible in one response and its prompt: purpose versus cause, recipient/beneficiary versus acting on someone’s behalf, duration versus deadline, route versus destination, payment/exchange, and suitability or reference. Many supplied corrections are preferences, unclear in context, or not reliably Por-vs-para contrasts, so they are assigned NONE. Unlike v1, this taxonomy has no codes for a learner’s general English-for mapping or inferred strategy, and it does not turn every conventional phrase into a separate code.
left_out: I left out global patterns such as English-for transfer, inconsistency across a learner’s history, avoidance, and lack of a stable system because they cannot be diagnosed from one response. I also left out a general fixed-expression code: items such as gracias por can be handled as conventional examples within the relevant meaning practice, not as evidence of a learner strategy. Several supplied changes appear preferential, unclear, or not actually a por/para contrast—especially some motion, votar por, buscar, and para/por occasion phrases—so those receive NONE rather than being forced into a code.

taxonomy.name: Purpose or goal versus cause or basis
taxonomy.definition: Use when the context clearly expresses a forward-looking purpose, intended result, or reason for doing something (para), but the learner uses por; or a cause, motive, stimulus, or basis (por), but the learner uses para. Includes emotional reactions to a stimulus and a basis for being famous, grateful, or rewarded. Do not use for a direct recipient/beneficiary, payment or exchange, or a person who is the standard for an evaluation.
positive_examples: Estudio por las clases [para las clases]: the classes are the purpose/context of study.
Estoy emocionada para ver [por ver] a mi familia: seeing them is the stimulus.
Es famoso para sus películas [por sus películas]: the films are the basis of his fame.
negative_examples: Compré un regalo por mi madre [para mi madre]: the mother is the recipient, not the cause.
Pagué para el libro [por el libro]: the phrase expresses payment, not purpose.

taxonomy.name: Recipient or beneficiary versus acting on someone’s behalf
taxonomy.definition: Use when a person or group is clearly the intended recipient or beneficiary of an item or action (para), but the learner uses por; or context clearly means doing something in someone’s place/on their behalf (por), but the learner uses para. Do not use for a general motive, a goal, suitability/reference, or an unclear phrase such as trabajar por alguien without enough context.
positive_examples: Compré un perro por mi madre [para mi madre]: she is the intended beneficiary.
Cocinaba desayuno por nuestra familia [para nuestra familia]: the family is who the breakfast is for.
Trabajé para él [por él]: when the context explicitly means acting in his place.
negative_examples: Estudio por mi familia [para mi familia only if they are recipients]: if they are the motive, this is a cause/motive contrast.
Este tamaño es perfecto por Maya [para Maya]: this is suitability/reference, not receipt.
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Contrast «Compré flores ___ Ana» (Ana receives them) with «Fui ___ Ana porque estaba enferma» (I went in her place).

taxonomy.name: Duration or time span versus deadline
taxonomy.definition: Use when a clearly stated length of time or period over which an event lasts calls for por (or a duration expression), but the learner uses para; or a clearly stated due date/deadline calls for para, but the learner uses por. Do not use for an approximate date, holiday occasion, or a phrase where duration versus deadline is not established.
positive_examples: Practiqué el fútbol para siete años [por siete años]: a length of time.
Estuve allí para tres años [por tres años]: a time span.
Quiero estar lista por el verano [para el verano]: a target time/deadline.
negative_examples: El informe es para el viernes: a deadline, correctly marked.
Nos vimos por Navidad: the occasion may allow more than one framing; do not code without clearer context.
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose: «Vivió allí ___ tres años» (duration) / «Entrega el trabajo ___ el viernes» (deadline).

taxonomy.name: Route or transit versus destination
taxonomy.definition: Use when the prompt clearly establishes movement through/along a route or area (por), versus movement toward a final destination (para), and the learner selects the other preposition. Do not use for a phrase that merely names a place after caminar or ir, since that can require a different construction or may be underspecified.
positive_examples: Pasamos para Córdoba [por Córdoba] antes de llegar a Sevilla: Córdoba is on the route.
Salimos por Madrid [para Madrid] como destino final: Madrid is the destination.
negative_examples: Fuimos a Granada para visitar la Alhambra: para marks purpose, not destination-versus-route.
Caminó por la biblioteca: por can correctly describe movement through a place.
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose: «Para llegar a Sevilla, pasamos ___ Córdoba» versus «El tren sale ___ Sevilla, su destino final».

taxonomy.name: Price, payment, or exchange
taxonomy.definition: Use when the intended relation is a price paid, payment for something, a reward, or an exchange (por), but the learner uses para. Do not use for the recipient of a purchase, the purpose of buying, or an ambiguous phrase about money without a clear transaction.
positive_examples: Pagaría para los asientos [por los asientos]: payment for the seats.
Vender los autógrafos para dinero [por dinero]: money received in exchange.
Ofrecían cuarenta mil dólares para su captura [por su captura]: a reward for the capture.
negative_examples: Compré un libro para mi hermano: the brother is the recipient.
Compré un libro para estudiar: studying is the purpose.
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose: «Te vendo la bicicleta ___ cien euros» (price/exchange) / «Compré la bicicleta ___ mi hermana» (recipient).

taxonomy.name: Suitability or reference point
taxonomy.definition: Use when para marks what is suitable, beneficial, difficult, important, or true from a stated person’s or thing’s point of view, but the learner uses por. Do not use when the person is simply a recipient, or when por clearly marks the cause or stimulus of an emotion.
positive_examples: Es una ventaja por mí [para mí]: the advantage is evaluated with respect to the speaker.
Era el tamaño perfecto por Maya [para Maya]: it suited Maya.
Es bueno por la salud [para la salud]: it is beneficial for health.
negative_examples: Estoy triste por mi amiga: she is the stimulus/cause of sadness, not a reference standard.
Compré ropa para mi madre: she is the recipient, not the evaluation point.
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose: «Es difícil ___ mí» (reference/experiencer) versus «Estoy triste ___ mí» meaning ‘because of myself’ (cause).
